value.summary: Build a donor management system for the non-profit sector, targeting launch in about three months. The brief lists OCR and image classification, search, native or cross-platform core flows, mapping, ERP exchange, privacy controls, security measures, REST APIs, reservations, dashboards, authentication including enterprise SSO, and high-fidelity design.

requirements.text: Extract fields from scanned documents using OCR.
Train or integrate a computer-vision model to classify uploaded images.
Provide a search results page with filters, sorting, and pagination.
Provide native or cross-platform screens for core user flows.
Provide map display, geocoding, and distance calculations.
Export orders to the ERP system and import stock levels from it.
Support consent management and data export and deletion requests.
Conduct an OWASP review and implement rate limiting and audit logging.
Provide REST endpoints for the main business entities, including validation.
Support availability rules, reservations, and conflict handling.
Provide a main dashboard with widgets, filters, and empty states.
Support registration, login, password reset, and email verification.
Support enterprise SSO login using the client's identity provider.
Produce high-fidelity mockups and component styles.
Target launch in about three months.
Prefer proven technology; budget is flexible.

ambiguities: The brief calls the product a donor management system, but mentions orders, stock levels, availability, and reservations without explaining how these relate to donor-management workflows.
The phrase “native/cross-platform” does not specify whether mobile apps, web screens, or both are required, nor which platforms must be supported.
The scope and expected accuracy of OCR and image classification are unspecified.
The ERP product, integration method, data formats, and synchronization expectations are unspecified.
The identity provider and required SSO protocol are unspecified.
The business entities, validation rules, user roles, and permissions are not defined.
The launch target is approximate, and the required launch scope or acceptance criteria are not stated.
assumptions: The listed bullets are intended as requested capabilities, but no detailed workflows or acceptance criteria are available.
The three-month target is a desired launch window rather than a guaranteed deadline.
“Budget is flexible” means there is no stated budget cap; it does not establish unlimited funding.
No specific technology stack is mandated; proven technology is a preference.
risks: The three-month target may be difficult to meet if all listed capabilities are required for launch, especially model work, ERP integration, SSO, and mobile delivery.
OCR and image-classification quality depends on representative documents and labeled image data, neither of which is described.
ERP and identity-provider dependencies may introduce access, compatibility, and coordination delays.
Unclear product scope around orders, stock, reservations, and donor management could cause substantial rework.
Privacy, security, and audit requirements may require additional legal, operational, or compliance decisions not specified in the brief.

unknowns.question: Does image classification require training a new model using client-provided labeled data, rather than integrating an existing model or service?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Training a model adds data preparation, labeling, experimentation, evaluation, and deployment work beyond a straightforward integration.

scenario_if_yes.title: Prepare and label image dataset for model training
Train, evaluate, and tune image classification model

unknowns.question: Are native or cross-platform mobile applications required in addition to web screens?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Mobile applications add platform-specific implementation, testing, and release work; the brief does not identify target platforms or clarify whether web is sufficient.

scenario_if_yes.title: Implement core user flows in a mobile application
Test mobile flows across target devices and platforms

unknowns.question: Does the client have an ERP with documented APIs and accessible test credentials for the required order and stock exchanges?
unknowns.why_it_matters: A supported API and timely access can make the integration relatively direct; absent or limited interfaces may require custom middleware, file exchange, or additional coordination.

scenario_if_yes.title: Build custom ERP integration or middleware for order and stock exchange

unknowns.question: Does the client require a specific identity provider or SSO protocol that is not supported by a standard integration?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nonstandard protocols or provider-specific requirements can add discovery, implementation, and testing effort beyond a conventional SSO setup.

scenario_if_yes.title: Implement and validate provider-specific SSO integration

unknowns.question: Are the scanned document types and required extracted fields known, and is a representative sample available?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Unknown document layouts or unavailable samples can require additional discovery, OCR configuration, and extraction validation.

scenario_if_yes.title: Discover document layouts and configure field extraction
